definitions.gloss: intractable disease; incurable illness; rare disease
definitions.explanation: A disease that is difficult to treat or cure, especially one officially designated as an intractable disease by the government. In Japan, the term is used both in everyday language and as an official medical/legal category for diseases eligible for government support.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{難病|なんびょう}と{闘|たたか}っている。
examples.english: She is fighting an intractable disease.

examples.japanese: {難病|なんびょう}{患者|かんじゃ}への{支援|しえん}{制度|せいど}が{拡充|かくじゅう}された。
examples.english: Support programs for patients with intractable diseases were expanded.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{治療法|ちりょうほう}の{開発|かいはつ}により、かつて{難病|なんびょう}とされた{病気|びょうき}が{治|なお}せるようになってきた。
examples.english: Thanks to the development of new treatments, diseases once considered intractable are becoming curable.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japan, {難病|なんびょう} has both a general meaning (any hard-to-cure disease) and an official designation under the {難病|なんびょう}{法|ほう} (Intractable Disease Act), which provides medical expense subsidies for patients with designated conditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {難病|なんびょう}と{闘|たたか}う (to fight an intractable disease)
- {難病|なんびょう}{患者|かんじゃ} (patient with an intractable disease)
- {難病|なんびょう}{指定|してい} (intractable disease designation)
- {難病|なんびょう}を{克服|こくふく}する (to overcome an intractable disease)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {難病|なんびょう}: intractable disease (hard to treat; may be officially designated)
- {不治|ふじ}の{病|やまい}: incurable illness (no known cure; literary)
- {持病|じびょう}: chronic illness (ongoing condition one lives with)
